{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABYyHulg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhCXh7U", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 29, "title": "Add bootable MSX floppy disk (DSK) support with an emulated disk controller and legal disk firmware", "body": "## Problem

The browser emulator can start MSX1/MSX2 Weave BASIC and many cartridge ROMs, including MegaROMs with SCC and SRAM, but **cannot mount or boot a floppy disk image**. A substantial category of MSX games and programs was distributed on floppies rather than cartridges. Merely accepting a `.dsk` upload is not sufficient: emulated Z80 software requires the drive/controller registers, disk interface ROM/BIOS services, correct slot mapping and a usable boot path.

The bundled C-BIOS is **cartridge-oriented and has no built-in disk ROM, Disk BASIC or MSX-DOS**. Do not assume that installing a DSK file alone will make disk programs run; do not silently substitute the custom Weave BASIC interpreter for genuine disk BIOS/OS services.

## Expected outcome

Visitors can **mount a standard raw `.dsk` floppy image in drive A:, boot appropriate disk software through an emulated MSX-compatible floppy controller and disk firmware, and interact with a program that is actually read from disk sectors by the Z80**. Provide one clear, end-to-end **independently authored, freely redistributable bootable disk demo** that works without any copyrighted Microsoft/ASCII/Konami firmware or commercial game assets.

Initial supported scope:
- Common raw 3.5-inch double-density **360 KiB (80 tracks, one side)** and **720 KiB (80 tracks, two sides)** DSK images, 9 sectors/track and 512 bytes/sector, with documented validation and media geometry. Standard additional geometries are optional; DMK/FDI and copy-protected/nonstandard track formats are out of scope.
- One emulated **drive A:** and one documented **WD2793-compatible** MSX disk-interface profile with a matching slot-visible disk-interface ROM. The exact documented register/slot wiring and firmware integration should be chosen together; there is no single universal MSX controller wiring.
- Read, seek, status/error handling and **write sector** support as required by the initial controller profile; explicit disk write protection and a safe means to preserve a modified DSK (at minimum **Export modified DSK**). No silent upload of disk data or unbounded host storage.
- **MSX2-first** browser boot path plus MSX1 support wherever this disk interface profile supports it. A diskless startup must continue to show the current model's Weave BASIC; loading ordinary cartridges must retain the existing automatic C-BIOS behavior. Clearly separate disk-capable boot mode from C-BIOS-only cartridge mode.

This milestone establishes working floppy hardware and a bootable, legal end-to-end example, **not universal compatibility with commercial disk games, MSX-DOS 1/2 or the full Disk BASIC command set**.

## Context and reproduction

- Repository: `takahirox/msx-rust`, default `main` at `6e010748c780` when drafted.
- Current modules: `crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs` models the Z80 bus, BIOS, slots and cartridge; `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs` exports the Wasm ABI; `web/app.js` provides file import and boot-policy controls; `scripts/build.sh` and `scripts/check-dist.mjs` manage independently licensed deployment assets.
- The current MSX2 profile has 64 KiB of fixed RAM, an expanded slot 3 with sub-ROM and RAM, and a bundled MSX2 C-BIOS main + sub-ROM. The disk interface must coexist with or explicitly and safely replace the relevant firmware/slot configuration, not overwrite or corrupt cartridge data or saved SRAM.
- Independent technical references:
  - [MSX raw DSK format and its limitations](https://www.msx.org/wiki/Emulation_related_file_formats)
  - [MSX disk sizes/geometry](https://www.msx.org/wiki/CALL_FORMAT)
  - [Disk-ROM BIOS calls (including DISKIO, DSKCHG, GETDPB)](https://direct.msx.org/wiki/Disk-ROM_BIOS)
  - [MSX disk interfaces and the distinction between C-BIOS and a disk ROM](https://direct.msx.org/forum/msx-talk/openmsx/openmsx-can-actually-boot-msx-dos1-with-c-bios-v029)
- Example reproduction now: fresh page → select MSX2 → try to mount a legally obtained raw `.dsk` image. There is no disk picker, no emulated floppy controller, no disk ROM and no boot-from-disk action.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Real disk hardware and boot path

- [ ] Implement a deterministic MSX floppy-drive image abstraction in the dependency-light Rust core: documented track/side/sector to byte offsets, drive ready/change/write-protect states, bounded sector transfers, malformed/truncated/unsupported geometry rejection and no out-of-bounds accesses. Support 360/720 KiB standard raw DSKs including 512-byte, 9-sector tracks.
- [ ] Implement one **documented WD2793-compatible FDC and MSX interface wiring** with Z80-visible register/slot access, drive/side/motor selection, seek/restore, sector read/write, command status, DRQ/IRQ or controller-equivalent transfer signaling, timeouts/errors and reset lifecycle as required for the selected profile. CPU software must access it through real emulated memory/I/O bus operations, not browser-simulated screen output or high-level shortcuts that bypass the controller.
- [ ] Provide a usable **Z80-executed disk-interface ROM/BIOS path** wired to the correct slots, disk detection and boot sequence. Ensure the standard disk entry points needed for the supported disk demo genuinely use the emulated FDC. Either independently author this redistributable firmware or obtain a verifiably redistributable existing disk-interface ROM and ship all its licenses/attributions/provenance. **Never bundle proprietary MSX disk BIOS, MSX-DOS system files, Microsoft BASIC, commercial disks, or copied proprietary ROM bytes.**
- [ ] Demonstrate a **complete disk boot** in MSX2: the Z80 runs the permitted boot/firmware chain, reads executable code or data from sectors in the mounted DSK, and produces verifiable on-screen output and keyboard-responsive behavior. Include an original bootable DSK plus source/build steps so all mandatory tests are independent of third-party game images. Exercise the compatible MSX1 path as well, or document a hardware/firmware-specific limitation accurately rather than pretending it works.
- [ ] Preserve **MSX2 as the initial browser machine** and Weave BASIC as the no-media default. Define deliberate, visible disk-vs-cartridge boot priority and slot ownership: mounting or ejecting a disk, changing machine/firmware, Reset and cartridge loading must not silently install an incompatible BIOS or discard an unrelated user-selected firmware override. Support a clear way to return to Weave BASIC. Avoid breaking the current MSX1/MSX2 C-BIOS and local firmware workflows.
- [ ] Implement sector writes to a **private writable mounted image copy** when write enabled, with read-only mode available. Provide a reliable **Export modified DSK** flow (preserving original geometry/bytes outside changed sectors), clear unsaved-change feedback and non-destructive Eject/Reset. Do not overwrite the user's original local file. No upload, analytics, service worker storage or arbitrary server-side data handling. Persistent local disk-image storage is not required for this first version.

### Browser UI, safety and tests

- [ ] Add a concise, accessible **Open DSK / Eject disk / Boot disk** workflow and disk status (drive A:, size, read-only/writable, unsaved modifications, errors) to the existing responsive page. Maintain the user-owned `Open ROM`, mapper picker, curated Demo ROMs and save-data workflows. Stage/validate the full DSK and required firmware resources **before committing** the changed machine; failed imports or unsupported formats must leave the running BASIC/cartridge, machine/firmware selection, SRAM and previous disk state unchanged.
- [ ] Preserve Wasm transfer memory safety, cancellation and concurrency protections; selecting a DSK, changing model, cartridge/firmware selection and rapid repeated operations must not race into a partial or inconsistent boot. Keep all file bytes in the browser, without logging source media contents. Show actionable unsupported-DSK errors.
- [ ] Add Rust unit/integration tests for controller commands/status, track/side/sector geometry, slot mapping, interrupts/transfer timing, media errors, write-protect, sector writes, boot/reset, no-media and changed/ejected disk behavior. Include an independent fixture proving real Z80 reads and writes sector content.
- [ ] Add Playwright tests on compiled Wasm at both `/` and `/msx-rust/` using the original DSK fixture: mount → controller/firmware boot → visible disk-loaded program → input response; modify and export DSK → verify exact sector changes; protect media; Reset/Eject; reject invalid DSKs; preserve previous session on failures. Test compatibility with MSX2-first initial BASIC, MSX1 mode, cartridge C-BIOS boot, mapper/SRAM saves, SCC audio, demos and local firmware. Neither a title-screen mockup nor successful file validation alone counts as disk-boot support.
- [ ] Update README, user help, disk controller/disk ROM design and provenance documentation with exact supported formats, geometry and boot limits. Explain that standard DSK images cannot represent arbitrary copy-protected tracks, that C-BIOS alone is not disk firmware, and that external disk games may require additional lawful BIOS/DOS/BASIC software that is **not bundled**.
- [ ] Run and accurately report `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs` and `npm test`. Follow the repository's English Issue → implementation → PR → AI review → revision → merge process. All mandatory pre-merge checks must be automated/AI-verifiable. Do not require proprietary disk images, subjective human gameplay, original Microsoft firmware or physical MSX hardware to approve the PR.

## Optional validation

The owner may try lawfully obtained commercial or freeware MSX1/MSX2 DSK images after merge and record whether they boot, load, use sound or write save data. Diagnose unsupported Disk BASIC/MSX-DOS dependencies, alternate FDC layouts, memory-mapper requirements and copy-protection as **separate follow-up Issues**. Do not claim arbitrary disk-game compatibility without evidence; physical-device and manual gameplay checks are optional.

## Required post-merge verification

- [ ] After merge and Pages deployment, verify the **actual published** https://takahirox.github.io/msx-rust/ site starts in MSX2 Weave BASIC, mounts and boots the original redistributable DSK fixture through the deployed Wasm/FDC/disk firmware, shows output responding to input, exports a disk whose changed sector bytes match expectations, and returns safely to BASIC when ejected. Record the deployment commit, successful Actions run, live site URL and observed results. This is strictly **post-merge**, not a pre-merge gate; report any failure as a separate Issue.
